document.executive_summary: This memo independently verifies the WO-03 selection. Recomputing from the trusted table: all four packages pass both gates (quality ≥80, defects ≤5), so ranking reduces to energy. Verified order: P3 10 Wh, P2 22, P1 28, P4 49 — gaps +12, +18 and +39 Wh above the minimum. The policy selects P3 outright. I audited A's brief claim by claim: gate values, gaps, consecutive spacing 12/6/21 Wh, cost ratios 2.2× and 4.9×, and risk margins all match the table without error. A correctly separates measured facts from open questions (P3 defect stability, batch-basis persistence, unverified cost and delivery, measurement uncertainty). My independent ballot is P3.
document.figure_caption: Verification view of WO-03: recomputed gate panel (all four pass) and energy ladder P3 10 Wh < P2 22 < P1 28 < P4 49, with gaps +12/+18/+39 Wh above the minimum.

recommendation.rationale: P3 is independently confirmed as the client winner: all gates pass, its 10 Wh measured energy is the lowest, and it leads runner-up P2 by 12 Wh on the identical basis. My recomputation matches A's arithmetic throughout; the 4/5 defect ceiling is a monitored contingency with P2 (22 Wh, zero defects) as fallback. Ballot: P3.

sections.body: The policy admits a package only at quality ≥80 and raw defects ≤5. From the trusted table: quality P4 98, P3 97, P2 95, P1 87 — all clear, with P1's margin smallest at +7. Defects: P1 0, P2 0, P4 2, P3 4 — all within 5, with P3 tightest at one defect of headroom. No package is excluded, so the lowest-ID tie-break never activates; selection reduces to minimizing measured energy. This reproduces A's gate panel exactly; I find no arithmetic error in A's eligibility table.
sections.heading: Eligibility gates recomputed

sections.body: Verified order on the shared acceptance-batch basis: P3 10 Wh < P2 22 < P1 28 < P4 49. Gaps above the minimum are +12, +18 and +39 Wh; consecutive spacing is 12, 6 and 21 Wh — a tight P2–P1 cluster and a wide P1–P4 tail. A's ratios also check: P2 costs 2.2× and P4 4.9× the 10 Wh minimum. No tie exists, so no tie-break applies. A's ladder statements match the trusted table, and the P3 recommendation follows directly from the energy-first policy with no discretionary quality weighting.
sections.heading: Energy ladder and gap audit

sections.body: Each decision-relevant claim was checked against the table. P3's defect margin: correct — it holds 4 of 5 permitted raw defects, so a regrade adding two or more disqualifies it and moves the win to P2 at 22 Wh with zero defects. P4: correct — even a clean regrade to zero defects cannot offset the 39 Wh penalty under the energy rule. P1: correct — 87 quality leaves a 7-point margin; P2's zero-defect record is the most regrade-robust. A properly flags cost, delivery, maintenance and field reliability as unverified rather than asserting them.
sections.heading: Claim-by-claim audit of A's brief

sections.body: Facts traced to the trusted table: every eligibility value, all four energies, and the gaps above. Open questions, unverified: (1) stability of P3's 4-defect count — the single decision-relevant uncertainty; (2) whether the shared batch basis persists across rounds; (3) any future cost or delivery evidence, which only the client could admit; (4) an uncertainty bound on the 10 Wh reading. Findings: A's brief is accurate, useful and correctly separates facts from questions. I confirm its recommendation; my independent ballot is P3, with no non-client endorsement.
